title: rdy/v1 run result
description: The JSON report rdy writes and Rdy Cloud reads. Ignore fields you do not know. Accept values not listed where a description says Open. Use verdict as written. A whole document is at most 2 MiB; readers should check that before parsing.

Action.description: One side effect, recorded as it happened. Fields beyond the required ones depend on kind.

check.description: Check key, or `null` for run level probes.

path.description: read, read_dir, stat, native, kube. Paths under a home directory start with ~.

name.description: env (the name only, never the value), dns

proto.description: connect: udp for a datagram exchange. Absent for a TCP connection.

of.description: coalesced: the kind that was coalesced

under.description: coalesced: the parent directory the file calls were under, or the program, host or path the other denied calls named, or * for denied calls past 100 targets

count.description: coalesced: how many calls the entry stands for. Reads past 200 per directory, or denied calls and failed file calls past 20 per parent directory (file calls) or target (other denied calls) and reason.

ActionKind.description: What a recorded side effect was. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

ActionOutcome.description: How a recorded side effect ended. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

Bucket.description:
The display group of a check, from the same rule as the verdict.

Sort by it in this order: blocker, required_not_run, warning, passed, not_applicable. Do not recompute it. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

Capability.description: One thing rdy probed before running checks, such as root or a reachable cluster.

hint.description: What to do when not available.

CheckResult.description: The outcome of one check entry.

key.description: `id`, or `id/name` when the spec gave a name. Unique in the report.

name.description: The spec's name for this entry, shown next to the id.

severity.description: From the spec. A value a consumer does not know counts as block. Open.

status.description: After severity is applied. An unknown status counts as not run. Open.

bucket.description: Display group, from the same rule as the verdict. Sort by it in this order: blocker, required_not_run, warning, passed, not_applicable. Do not recompute it. Open.

skip_kind.description: Present when `status` is `skipped`. `not_applicable` comes only from the spec's `os` list. A check that cannot work on this OS is `not_yet_on_os`. Open.

unsupported_fields.description: For `unsupported_spec`: the fields this rdy could not read.

message.description: One line, at most 1 KiB, such as `15.4 GiB found, 32 GiB needed`.

fix.description: What to do. `null` only for pass and not applicable.

fix_source.description: Whose fix text `fix` is: `spec` is the vendor's text, `rdy` is rdy's own. `null` on pass. Open.

builtin_fix.description: rdy's text when the spec's fix replaced it.

observed.description: Measured values, at most 64 KiB. Keys are per check id, in snake_case, with the unit in the name (`_bytes`, `_ms`, `_percent`). Keys are only ever added.

expected.description: Thresholds that applied after defaults. Same rules as `observed`.

needs.description: Hard and soft needs the check declared, and whether each was met.

partial.description: Set when some sources could not be read. A partial check never blocks on data it could not read.

notes.description: Up to 20 notes of 1 KiB each.

ErrorKind.description: Why a check ended in `error`. Present when the status is `error`. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

ErrorOutput.description: Not a report. What rdy prints on stdout with --json when it exits 64 or 70 without a verdict. api_version and kind are written but not required.

code.description: Stable code: usage, spec_unreadable, spec_parse, spec_invalid, spec_unsigned, spec_signature_invalid, spec_key_unknown, spec_expired, trust_store_insecure, report_write, interrupted, internal. Open.
The code: `unknown_key`, `unknown_check`, `unsupported_field`, `bad_value`, `not_in_build`, `no_threshold` or `structure`. The set only grows.

line.description: The line in the file, from 1, when it is known.

column.description: The column in the file, from 1, when it is known.

key.description: The key of the check the finding is about (`host.disk` or `host.disk/data`). Null for a finding about the file as a whole.

message.description: What is wrong. Safe to print: text from the file is cut and escaped.

fix.description: What to do about it. Never empty.

FixSource.description: Whose fix text a result carries. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

Host.description: The machine, coarsely. No MAC addresses, environment values, command line, working directory, home paths, kubeconfig contents, raw machine id or serial numbers.

host_id.description: First 16 hex digits of an HMAC-SHA256 of the OS machine id with key `rdy-host-id-v1` plus the product. The same host and product give the same value. Different products give unrelated values. `null` when there is no usable machine id (macOS for now).

virtualization.description: Whether the host is a virtual machine.

container.description: rdy ran inside a container or WSL.

HostOs.description: The operating system of the host.

HostOsFamily.description: The OS family of the host. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

euid.description: Effective uid on Unix, `null` on Windows.

elevated.description: Effective uid 0 on Unix, a high integrity token on Windows.

kube.description: The Kubernetes identity in use. `null` when no k8s check ran.

KubeIdentity.description: The Kubernetes identity of a run.

user.description: The authenticated user from `SelfSubjectReview`. When that API is missing or the call fails, the user entry named in the kubeconfig context, with `user_verified` false.

user_verified.description: `true` when `user` came from `SelfSubjectReview`. `false` when it is the kubeconfig user, which the API server did not verify.

exec_plugin.description: Base name of the kubeconfig credential plugin that ran, if any.

oneOf.description: Lint exits 1 and sign goes on.

LintReport.description:
Not a `Report`. What `rdy spec lint` prints with `--json`.

The counts equal the number of findings of each level.

file.description: The file as the caller named it.

findings.description: Every finding, in file order. Empty when the spec is clean.

Need.description: Something rdy needs for a check, such as root or a cluster. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

NeedState.description: A need a check declared and whether it was met.

hard.description: `true`: the check does not run without it. `false`: it runs partial.

OpenCode.description: A snake_case code. Newer producers may send values not listed.

Partial.description: Which sources a check could not read.

note.description: What is missing, or the OS note for a `Partial` OS.

Producer.description: The rdy build that wrote a report.

commit.description: Short git commit of the build.

rdy_spec.description: Version of the rdy-spec crate that wrote this file.

Proxy.description: Proxy settings in effect, user info stripped from URLs.

Redaction.description: What the redactor changed in a report. Counts only, never the matched text.

RedactionRuleset.description: Which compiled redaction rule set ran. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

Report.description: One run of rdy run: who ran what, where, and what came of it. Ignore fields you do not know. Use verdict as written.

producer.description: The rdy build that wrote this.

run.description: When and how the run went.

proxy.description: Proxy settings in effect, user info stripped. `null` when none.

capabilities.description: Every need rdy probed before running checks, and the result.

verdict.description: The overall answer. Closed in v1: a new verdict value needs `rdy/v2`. Use it as written.

verdict_reason.description: Set when the verdict is not explained by an observed block or warning. `required_check_not_run` means NOT READY with no block. `nothing_verified` means READY with warnings because no check reached pass, warn or block. Otherwise `null`. Open.

exit_code.description: The exit code for this verdict: 0, 1 or 2. When rdy cannot write the report it exits 70 instead and `complete` is false.

checks.description: One entry per spec check, in spec order. Sort by bucket for display.

actions.description: Every file read, command, lookup, connection and API request, in order. At most 5000 entries.

actions_truncated.description: `true` when the log dropped an entry: at the 5000 entry cap or a check's 1000 entry quota. `ok` then `failed` `read`, `read_dir` and `stat` entries go first. A `denied` entry is never dropped for another kind of entry, and repeated denials fold into one `coalesced` entry per parent directory (file calls) or per target (other calls).

actions_dropped.description: How many entries of each kind were dropped. `read`, `read_dir`, `stat` and `coalesced` entries are dropped first; any other kind only as a last resort.

redaction.description: What the redactor changed in this report.

complete.description: `false` when rdy could not finish or write the report (exit 70).

Run.description: When a run happened and the options it ran with.

options.description: The options that shaped the run.

RunOptions.description: The options of a run that change what a reader should expect.

jobs.description: Checks that ran at once, 1 to 32.

network.description: `false` when sockets were turned off for this run.

Severity.description:
How much a check matters, as the spec wrote it.

An unknown severity counts as `block` everywhere. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

Signature.description: Who signed the spec, as far as rdy could tell.

state.description: `verified` is signed by a trusted key. `unsigned` is no signature, run with `--allow-unsigned`. `invalid` appears only in the `rdy verify` object, never in a report. Open: treat an unknown value as not verified.

key_id.description: Minisign key id, 16 uppercase hex digits.

key_fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the 32 byte ed25519 public key, 64 hex digits. The key id alone is not an identity.

product.description: Product from the signed trusted comment.

trust_note.description: The local note from the trust store entry. Never text from the spec.

trust_source.description: Where the key came from: the system or user trust store, or `flag` for a key given with `--key` for one run. Open: treat an unknown value like `flag`.

SignatureState.description:
The state of the spec signature in a report.

An unknown state counts as not verified. `invalid` appears in the `rdy verify` object, never in a written report. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

SkipKind.description:
Why a check did not run. Present when the status is `skipped`.

Every kind except `not_applicable` counts as not run, and so does an unknown kind. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

SpecRef.description: Which spec ran: the signed metadata and the hash of the exact bytes.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact bytes that were verified and parsed, 64 lowercase hex digits.

file_name.description: Base name only, never the full path.

Status.description:
What happened to a check, after its severity was applied.

An unknown status counts as not run. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

Summary.description:
Counts of the results.

`pass + warn + block + skipped + timeout + error = total` for every result whose status is known. `skipped` counts every `status: skipped` entry, not applicable included. `not_applicable`, `required_not_run` and `optional_not_run` are views inside that sum. A result whose status this version does not know counts in `total` and in `required_not_run` or `optional_not_run` only. The summary may gain keys, so never sum every key.

skipped.description: Every result with status `skipped`, not applicable included.

not_applicable.description: Skipped because the spec's `os` list leaves this OS out. Never counts toward the verdict.

required_not_run.description: Severity block (or unknown) and not run.

TrustSource.description:
Where the trusted key came from.

An unknown source is treated like `flag`. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

Verdict.description: The overall answer of a run. Closed in v1: a new value needs `rdy/v2`.

oneOf.description: Everything the spec asks for passed. Exit 0.
Warnings only, or optional checks did not run, or nothing was verified. Exit 1.
A block, or a required check did not run. Exit 2.

VerdictReason.description: Why the verdict is not explained by an observed block or warning. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.

Verification.description: Not a report. What rdy verify prints with --json when the spec is accepted.

Version.description:
The `rdy` binary's own identity, as `rdy version --json` prints it.

Like the other `rdy/v1` objects it only grows: a later release may add fields, and a reader ignores the ones it does not know. `commit` and `date` are `null` when the build had no trustworthy git information, for example a build from a source tarball.

version.description: Version of the rdy binary, such as `0.1.0` or `0.1.0-alpha.3`.

commit.description: Short git commit of the build: the first 7 hex digits of the hash.

date.description: Date of that commit in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

target.description: Rust target triple the binary was built for.

rdy_spec.description: Version of the rdy-spec crate inside this binary.

api_version.description: The wire format this binary reads and writes. Always `rdy/v1` in this release line.

Virtualization.description: Whether the host is a virtual machine. Open: a newer producer may send other snake_case values.
